title: [Lean] Recover compact dictionary values from original bytes and keys
body:
Author-checked kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918. This reusable Lean chunk preserves that selected-result context and does not change the exponent.

Three checked modules derive a compact dictionary certificate from original artifact bytes and an ordered key witness. HexObjectLayout derives exact selected offsets and slices from complete ordered layout. CheckedCompactObject checks all original bytes against compact Nat-column payloads and actual parser/recovery. KeyOnlyCompactObject obtains all column values internally from actual named lookups, then derives the restricted independent column operator and both inverse identities on success.

## Verified coverage

Finite coverage: arbitrary binary dimension and finite field lists, unique nonempty lowercase-hex keys and complete byte-layout equality. No selected-file census or successful ACTUAL-SIGMAS artifact execution is claimed.

Conditional-interface coverage: actual checker success implies the recovered restricted column certificate. Completeness retains whole-artifact/fragment parser equations, per-field decoding, full-layout/key policy and the restricted single-transvection/permutation Candidate check. Key order remains an explicit witness. No target operator equality is assumed.

Full-theorem coverage: no installed parser internal span/pre-collapse proof, file/digest authentication, general JSON round trip, runtime extern refinement, complex phase, physical execution/cost, recursive all-size bound or full multiplication theorem.

## Exact sources and reproducibility

Three new accepted sources, 30,214 bytes, reuse twenty unchanged public prerequisites. Eight changed files total; no prerequisite source copies. All three sources have fresh bounded local kernel checks and independent source/API/terminal acceptance: seventeen complete standard-axiom probes and six full printed types, with no accepted diagnostic or admitted proof. Historical preparation comments remain byte-for-byte and are qualified by ACCEPTANCE.json. REPRODUCTION.md is a prospective recipe for the pinned Lean 4.21.0 and Mathlib environment, not a publication-time replay or CI-pass claim.

The manifest retains directly author-checked main 299eb8effe080183313757ac36e76c1b98ed9fae and its source-matched kappa. Candidate parent is 94e50883325b387add6891258a986f797b09cacc. Fresh scoped checks at 808a78151fa2da6865c33a8a0f4c0a6ff78bd5f4 confirm the same five critical scientific source blobs; the complete fe19567-to-808 comparison has 38 commits and 231 changed files with no Lean source changes. New unrelated fixtures are not accepted suppliers.

## Reuse and attribution

Compared direct predecessors PR1831, PR1879, PR1927, PR1950, PR1961 and PR1978. The new complete-layout proof derives containment; the key-only layer removes supplied column values. Exact module searches found no duplicate PR. OVERLAP.md and PUBLIC_SOURCE_MANIFEST.json give the bounded comparison and immutable dependencies without claiming global novelty.

Credits: James Chang with OpenAI assistance; Lean/Mathlib authors; Jeremy Kothe T16/PR514; Rohan Arun PR1094; and the accepted strict-decoder, slice, compact-column and restricted-certificate components. Existing source attribution and Apache-2.0 notices are preserved.

Submission context: five critical inputs also freshly match at 697b00e5d36297563c22aac080dd5dee398c2624; exact fork head e7dc7c13a63043a0ebbbadc8cf686d858ecc5516.
